title: No metrics in your job? Here's what to do... (Resume Advice)
description:
How can you add metrics to your resume to show marketable value if you job doesn’t directly operate with numbers? Our biggest advice for addressing this is realizing what can all count as a metric, moving from company level achievements to personal level, and address things on a shorter time instance. Did you complete a project earlier than expected? Did you have the biggest social reach month the company has ever seen? Have you gotten faster at your job the longer you’ve been there? These are all questions to ask yourself about how to find these metrics and achievements. #resumebullets #resumetips #resumeadvice #resume #resumetemplate #resumewriting

transcript: How do you add numbers to your resume if your job doesn't deal with metrics? The first thing is realizing how much can actually count as a metric. It's not just revenue or sales. Something like time is a common factor with every job. Are you doing the same thing that you did last month but faster this month? That's an achievement. Rough percentages, that's another way you can do things. And looks really good because increasing something from five to 10 might not sound good, but a 100% increase always does. And then also think about a shorter timetable for your achievements. Maybe year-over-year is you don't know that, but maybe you do have a better idea of month-over-month, week-over-week, or just day-to-day.
